newsitem.title: USA: Man arrested for Southwest Airline bomb threat.
newsitem.headline: Man arrested for Southwest Airline bomb threat.

text.p: A Southwest Airlines Co. jet made an unscheduled landing in Pensacola on Friday after a passenger said he found a note saying a bomb on the plane was about to explode, Pensacola police said.
Southwest flight 475, en route from New Orleans to Orlando, was diverted to land at the nearby Pensacola Regional Airport at 8:15 a.m. CST (1415 GMT).
All 39 passengers and five crew members aboard the Boeing 737 were evacuated safely, a police spokeswoman said.
Police said passenger Frank Lopez, 28, was questioned after the landing and arrested and charged with providing false information and making a threat.

Lopez, who is a steward for Amtrak, told a flight attendant during the flight he found the bomb threat note in a seat pocket. The flight attendant immediately gave the note to the pilot, who requested permission to land at the nearest airport, police said.
Two bomb-sniffing dogs from the local sheriff's office investigated the aircraft after it landed, but found no evidence of a bomb.
Lopez could face up to five years in prison if convicted of the charges.
